prompt: A storage tank is being filled by a pipe at a rate of 15 liters per minute while a leak drains it at 4 liters per minute. If the tank currently holds 200 liters and its capacity is 500 liters, calculate how many minutes it will take to reach full capacity.
evaluation_criteria:
Net Rate Calculation: 0-5 (Evaluates correct net fill rate computation)
Time To Capacity: 0-5 (Evaluates correct division of remaining volume by net rate)
response_text:
To find out how many minutes it will take to fill the tank, we can follow these steps:

1. **Calculate the net rate at which the tank is filling:**
   $$\text{Net rate} = \text{Inflow rate} - \text{Leak rate}$$
   $$\text{Net rate} = 15\text{ liters/minute} - 4\text{ liters/minute} = 11\text{ liters/minute}$$

2. **Calculate the remaining volume needed to reach full capacity:**
   $$\text{Volume needed} = \text{Total capacity} - \text{Current volume}$$
   $$\text{Volume needed} = 500\text{ liters} - 200\text{ liters} = 300\text{ liters}$$

3. **Calculate the time required:**
   $$\text{Time} = \frac{\text{Volume needed}}{\text{Net rate}}$$
   $$\text{Time} = \frac{300}{11}\text{ minutes}$$

$$\text{Time} \approx 27.27\text{ minutes}$$

It will take **$27\frac{3}{11}$ minutes** (or approximately **27 minutes and 16 seconds**) to reach full capacity.
